summary.headline: Amanta Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR83.1 crore with EBITDA margin of 21.6%; SteriPort Line 3 commissioned, taking capacity to about INR11.6 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR83.1 crore, up 17% YoY, with EBITDA up about 22% to INR18 crore at a 21.6% margin and PAT of INR4.86 crore, up 26%. H1 FY27 revenue was INR151.9 crore (up 12%), EBITDA INR33 crore (up 8%) and PAT INR8.17 crore (up 12%). SteriPort Line 3 was commissioned in early September 2026, and management reiterated FY27 revenue of INR420-430 crore on an annualised run-rate basis. Polymer price volatility was absorbed in the quarter, with price increases of about 4-4.5% taken across products; the SVP expansion has slipped from Feb-Mar 2027 to a Q1 FY28 start.

financial_highlights.value: about INR190 crore incl. about INR45 crore working capital

segments.name: SteriPort (2-port ISBM IV fluid)
segments.commentary: Capacity raised about 75% from INR6.6 crore to about INR11.6 crore per year with Line 3 at Kheda; Line 3 was running at about 55% in early November and management expects full utilisation from 20 November. Line 3 is expected to contribute about INR60 crore of revenue in FY27, with the INR110 crore annual run-rate guidance dependent on optimal utilisation.

segments.name: Small volume parenterals (SVP)
segments.commentary: SBU revenue is about INR55-65 crore; capacity to rise about 52% from INR20.9 crore to about INR31 crore in Q1 FY28, dedicated mainly to inhalation (BFS) and preservative-free ophthalmics. Management is targeting INR16 crore of SVP revenue in FY28 as a conservative figure, with a wider INR35-60 crore range cited as speculative.

segments.name: Legacy / classic pack and licensing
segments.commentary: Management said contract and licensing revenue is about 2-3% of revenue, roughly INR25-30 crore for the year. International revenue was about 32% of Q2 FY27 revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at about INR420-430 crore on an annualised basis, with Q3 and Q4 at the same run-rate as Q2.
Two-year aim of 20%-plus revenue CAGR and 25%-plus EBITDA margins.
Gross margin and product-mix benefits expected to show in Q3 and Q4 FY27, despite the SVP line being about 5 months late.
Power savings from the 10.8 MW captive solar plant estimated at about INR9 crore per year.

Debt expected at about INR130 crore term loan plus working capital (about INR175-180 crore total) by end FY27; annual repayment about INR30-35 crore; term loans about INR100 crore plus about INR50 crore working capital in roughly two years.
Polymer prices expected to normalise in 3-6 months; if oil returns to pre-conflict levels, plastic cost could fall further.
capex_capacity: SteriPort Line 3 commissioned in first week of September 2026; running at about 55% in early November, full capacity targeted from 20 November 2026 (45-60 days ramp).

SVP expansion: capacity from INR20.9 crore to about INR31 crore; machine FAT slipped about one month to 13-19 December, equipment expected January, commissioning by end-March 2027, revenue from Q1 FY28.
Utilisation of existing plant about 95-97%; no near-term SteriPort capex planned given 12 crore SteriPort plus about 6 crore legacy pack capacity.

Future capex mainly product development, dossiers, and plant automation, about INR7-20 crore per item; a glass-based injectable line (vials, ampoules, cartridges) was mentioned as a long-term idea costing well below INR120 crore.
10.8 MW captive solar plant generating since end of Q1 FY27; solar term loan interest already flowing through finance cost.
demand_pricing: Price increases of about INR0.70 to INR1.80 per bottle (average about INR1, or about 4-4.5%) taken to offset polymer price spikes; polymer prices rose more than 70% at one point and have been volatile.
Estimated share of Indian IV fluid market: about 6% for SteriPort alone and about 2.5-3% for BFS; India IV fluid market about 190-200 crore units.
Channel network of about 200-250 partners nationwide after SteriPort enabled pan-India distribution; SteriPort focus on ICU, onco, intensive cardiac, paediatrics, anaesthesia.
Management claims over 35 crore SteriPort bottles marketed since 2016 with no fungal contamination complaints received.

Inhalation pipeline of 20 products (about 12 in SVP); 2 inhalation products commercialised; filing in advanced markets to start January-February 2027. Budesonide suspension validation batch completed in the quarter.
Management expects NPPA/NLEM distribution-margin reforms to hit hospital retail margins rather than manufacturer margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is current plant utilisation and target for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall plant utilisation about 95-97%; Line 3 at about 55%, expected to reach full capacity from 20 November, with all lines at 100% thereafter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall while EBITDA held steady?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it absorbed polymer price volatility (over 70% spike at one point), passed on price increases and mix benefits; it expects margin normalisation in 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current net debt and repayment plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Total borrowings about INR190 crore at September end including about INR45 crore working capital; expected about INR130 crore term debt plus working capital at end FY27; annual repayment about INR30-35 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 include SVP contribution and how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; SVP is conservatively taken at INR16 crore of FY28 revenue, with management calling higher figures (INR35-60 crore) speculative; numbers to be shared in about 15 days.

qa_highlights.question: Is SteriPort exported to Australia and Canada?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected that Canada and Australia received diluents, not SteriPort; SteriPort is India-centric, and freed-up capacity could target advanced markets once inhalation moves to the new SVP line.

qa_highlights.question: Is further SteriPort capex planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No immediate plan; current 12 crore SteriPort plus 6 crore legacy capacity is seen as sufficient for hospital demand; SVP is the mid-term focus.

risks_watch: Polymer (oil-linked) price volatility; margin uplift depends on normalisation in 3-6 months.
SteriPort Line 3 ramp to 100% by 20 November and ramp to INR60 crore in FY27 and INR110 crore run-rate.
SVP commissioning slipped by about a month on FAT and is targeted for March 2027; tech transfer for suspension products may take 6-7 months and inhalation variations 6-9 months.
Management declined to quantify SVP FY28 revenue and margins; a detailed three-year simulation was promised within about 15 days.
Regulatory price-control reforms (NPPA/NLEM) on distribution margins.
Dependence on hospital channel adoption of premium SteriPort product.
summary.management_tone: Confident on delivery and near-term numbers, with the 20%-plus CAGR and 25%-plus margin aims stated firmly. Noticeably cautious and hedged on SVP revenue, utilisation and timelines, repeatedly calling figures speculative and promising follow-up numbers later.
key_quotes: Q2 FY '27 has been a quarter of delivery for Amanta. Our top line grew by 17% year-on-year and profit grew even faster than revenue.
SteriPort is primarily India-centric activity, and SVP capacity that we are creating, right now inhalation products are made on one line.
And gain, it is very -- I would say it is very speculative to give number at this stage because, for one, the utilization is going to be very, very low.

adds.what: SteriPort Line 3 at Kheda (ISBM IV fluid), lifting SteriPort capacity from INR6.6 crore to about INR11.6 crore per year
SVP expansion, capacity from INR20.9 crore to about INR31 crore (inhalation BFS and preservative-free ophthalmics)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR420-430 crore annualised (implied ~15% growth off H1 run-rate of INR151.9 crore, which is a lower bar than it sounds), backed by SteriPort Line 3 (capacity up ~75%, ~INR60 crore FY27 contribution, ramp to full utilisation from 20 Nov) and pricing of ~4-4.5%; however the SVP expansion slipped to Q1 FY28 and existing plant is at 95-97% utilisation.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects gross margin and product-mix benefits in Q3 and Q4 FY27 and polymer normalisation in 3-6 months, against a 21.6% Q2 EBITDA margin and 2-year aim of 25%-plus.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: SteriPort Line 3 already commissioned (capacity to about INR11.6 crore, up 75%) and ramping to full use from 20 Nov; SVP capacity from INR20.9 crore to about INR31 crore (52%) commissioning by end-March 2027 with revenue from Q1 FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Plant utilisation at 95-97% with Line 3 at about 55% ramping to full, expected to add about INR60 crore of SteriPort revenue in FY27 and FY27 guidance of INR420-430 crore annualised versus H1 run-rate of INR151.9 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management sees no near-term SteriPort capex given 12 crore plus 6 crore legacy capacity, with only INR7-20 crore product-development and automation items; yet 95-97% utilisation keeps a later glass-line idea open.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR420-430 crore annualised with Q3 and Q4 at Q2 run-rate (about INR83 crore a quarter), and Line 3 ramp could beat the INR60 crore FY27 contribution, but SVP upside is called speculative.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Polymer costs rose more than 70% at one point and are volatile, SVP has already slipped about 5 months, and Line 3 ramp to full use is only targeted from 20 Nov at about 55% now.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Inhalation pipeline of 20 products with 2 commercialised, filings in advanced markets from Jan-Feb 2027, and SVP (BFS inhalation and preservative-free ophthalmics) starting from Q1 FY28, though variations take 6-9 months.

rows.label: Polymer cost normalisation and price pass-through
rows.why: Management expects polymer prices to normalise in 3-6 months and price rises of about 4-4.5% were taken, so margin could expand if oil-linked costs fall further, but this depends on oil.

rows.label: Debt reduction to about INR175-180 crore total by end FY27
rows.why: Total borrowings about INR190 crore in Sep 2026 with annual repayment of about INR30-35 crore, so debt falls as cash flow covers repayments.

rows.label: NPPA/NLEM distribution-margin reforms
rows.why: Management expects reforms to hit hospital retail margins rather than manufacturer margins, but the impact on SteriPort's premium hospital channel is not quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on Line 3 ramp, the INR420-430 crore FY27 guide and the 20%-plus CAGR aim, but cautious and hedged on SVP revenue, utilisation and timelines, calling higher figures speculative. Analysts probed on the gross-margin fall, debt repayment and SVP FY28 contribution.
